Package com.epitech.depthdiablo.engine

Class World

java.lang.Object
com.epitech.depthdiablo.engine.World
All Implemented Interfaces:
Rewindable
public final class World extends Object implements Rewindable
Holds everything alive during one run and advances it, one logic tick at a time. Owns the EventBus of the run (GDD 1.1.2).

    • add

      public void add(Entity entity)
      Adds an entity to the world. During a tick, the entity joins at the end of that tick, so it is first updated on the next one.
      Parameters:
      entity - the entity to add
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the entity is null

    • tick

      public void tick()
      Advances the world by one tick: updates every entity, tells every pair of overlapping entities that they touch, delivers the queued events, then adds the waiting entities and drops the removed ones.

    • isFree

      public boolean isFree(Aabb box, Entity mover)
      Tells wether a mover can stand in the given box: no other blocking entity overlaps it. A mover cheks the box before moving, so walls, closed doors and chest stop it (GDD 1.5).
      Parameters:
      box - the box the mover whant to occupy
      mover - the entity that wants to move there; it never blocks itself
      Returns:
      thrue if no blocking entity other than the mover overlaps the box
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if box or mover is null

    • isFree

      public boolean isFree(Obb shape, Entity mover)
      Tells whether a turned shape touches no wall, such as the next hitbox of a projectile.
      Parameters:
      shape - the shape to check
      mover - the entity that would stand there; never a wall to itself
      Returns:
      true if no blocking entity overlaps the shape
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null

    • writeState

      public void writeState(StateBuffer out)
      Takes the photo of the whole world for R (GDD 1.1.2): the tick number, then for every entity the entity itself and its own state. Keeping the entities themselves is what lets a rewind bring back a dead one and drop one spawned since.
      Specified by:
      writeState in interface Rewindable
      Parameters:
      out - the photo being taken
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if called during a tick, when the world is half updated

    • readState

      public void readState(StateBuffer in)
      Puts the world back as it was in the photo: the tick number, the list of entities rebuilt from the photo, each with its state. Events still queued belong to the undone future, so they are dropped.
      Specified by:
      readState in interface Rewindable
      Parameters:
      in - the photo being restored
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if called during a tick
